newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end at day's lows, mood still bearish.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end at day's lows, mood still bearish.

text.p: Italian stocks ended at day's lows on Wednesday, continuing a technical correction, with widespread selling seen in a market searching for direction, traders said. Weak bond futures and an easier lira weighed on sentiment.

A good part of trade was accounted for by futures arbitrage. "There's nothing to carry the market further at the moment. The question is whether the bubble has burst or are we waiting for a new wave of enthusiasm," one trader said.
The All-share Mibtel index closed down 2.25 percent at a session low of 12,199 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended down 2.66 percent down at a 18,140 low for the day.

News Olivetti saw a 1996 pretax loss of around 800 billion lire with sales down 16 percent came in after the market had closed. The stock had ended 0.91 percent off at 646 lire but off a session low of 625 on a bit of shortcovering ahead of board meeting on results.

Noting generally weaker European stock markets, one dealer said he had heard rumours of pan-European selling programmes but said the international retail investor was not really in the Italian market.
The market had ticked up slightly in line with Wall Street on benign December durable goods orders but then collapsed.

"Sell into strength seems to be the byword as opposed to buy on the back of nothing," said Oriano Moro of Gestnord brokers. "Everyone said the market could do with a breather, and it could drift down a bit further. All the good news is priced in but we could spark up just as easily," he said.
"There's no lack of liquidity and it won't take much for the market to get going again," another trader said.
Profit-taking particularly hit telecoms, Eni and Fiat. Eni ended 2.05 percent down at 8,737 lire and Fiat lost 1.51 percent to 5,224.
In telecoms, Stet holding lost 2.88 percent to 7,699, Telecom Italia shed 3.41 percent to 4,499 and mobile phone operator TIM lost 2.63 percent to 4,735 lire.
Against the trend, former Olivetti chairman Carlo De Benedetti's CIR industrial holding company gained 5.86 percent to 1,156 lire.
